name: Noxian podium

intent.purpose: Establish place, power and the setup of a public trial.
intent.reason: The fortress gives Noxus its weight, and that weight makes the later pettiness funny.
intent.attention: Fortress first, then the bench and podium, then the watching citizens.
intent.relationships: State power towers over a modest public proceeding, and the citizens are its audience.

staging.positions: The bench and podium face each other in the square, with the citizens at its edge.
staging.camera: A slow, steady tilt down from the skyline to a wide, then a hold.

editorial.cutOut: Cut on the settled wide to a closer lateral view once Riley is brought in.
editorial.timing: An unhurried, grand rhythm to set up the comic deflation.

advanced.assumptions: The fortress is placed behind the bench as a staging assumption.

shots.title: Shadow of Noxus
shots.sourceExcerpt: A judicial bench and battered defendant’s podium occupy a sunlit square. Three curious citizens stop to watch. Beyond the rooftops, an enormous black fortress dominates the skyline, its battlements bristling with crimson banners.
shots.description: Opening composition: the enormous black fortress fills the upper frame above sunlit rooftops, its battlements bristling with crimson banners stirring in the wind. The camera tilts down and settles on a wide view of the square. An empty judicial bench and a battered defendant's podium stand in the sunlight. Three curious citizens stop at the edge of the square to watch. Ending composition: a static wide tableau of bench, podium and onlookers, with the fortress still looming behind.
shots.atmosphere: Bright, dry daylight; the fortress is ominous and heavy against an otherwise ordinary public square; ambient murmur and wind in banners.
shots.music: A solemn, overblown imperial brass swell that sounds a little too grand for the small trial below.

intent.purpose: Show that Riley wants out and cannot leave.
intent.reason: A single lateral take lets the escape attempt and the casual block play as one clean gag.
intent.attention: Riley's sidelong move toward the passage, then the chair sliding into her path.
intent.relationships: The guard controls Riley effortlessly, without even looking at her.

staging.positions: The podium sits centre, the guard's chair beside it and the passage to one side.
staging.facing: The guard looks down throughout and never at Riley.
staging.movement: Riley is placed, edges sideways, is blocked and returns.
staging.camera: A locked-off lateral frame so the geography of the escape route reads clearly.

editorial.cutIn: Moves from the grand wide to a ground-level comic frame.
editorial.cutOut: Cut once she is back at the podium, to the magistrate taking his seat of authority.
editorial.timing: Hold a beat after the chair stops before Riley gives up.

advanced.continuity: The chair stays positioned blocking the passage for the rest of the scene.
advanced.assumptions: The passage being on the guard's side is a staging assumption.

shots.title: No Exit
shots.sourceExcerpt: The guard places Riley behind the podium. She edges toward an open passage. Without looking up, he slides his chair into her path. She returns to the podium.
shots.description: Opening composition: a lateral medium-wide at waist height that frames the podium, the guard's chair beside it and the open passage at the frame's edge. The guard steers Riley into place behind the podium. He sits. Riley glances at the passage and edges sideways toward it. Without looking up, the guard slides his chair into her path, and it stops squarely in front of her. A beat. She walks back to the podium. Ending composition: Riley back behind the podium, the guard seated and impassive, the passage now blocked by his chair.
shots.atmosphere: Dry, deadpan physical comedy in bright sun.
shots.music: The brass fades out to near silence so the chair scrape lands.

intent.purpose: Introduce the judge and the first, serious-sounding charge.
intent.reason: The low angle builds his authority so the tiny glasses can puncture it.
intent.attention: The armor, then the glasses, then his reading.
intent.relationships: He is the authority Riley must answer to, imposing but faintly absurd.

staging.eyelines: Down to his papers, not yet at Riley.
staging.camera: A static, low frontal medium shot.

editorial.cutIn: Cut from Riley's defeat to the person who will judge her.
editorial.cutOut: Cut on the interruption at the dash, to a two-shot as Riley cuts in.
editorial.timing: Let the glasses business take its time before the line.

advanced.continuity: The glasses stay on for the rest of the scene.

shots.title: The Tiny Glasses
shots.sourceExcerpt:
A NOXIAN MAGISTRATE sits behind the bench, armored in black iron. He puts on very small reading glasses.

### MAGISTRATE

You entered Noxus under suspicious circumstances—
shots.description: Opening composition: a frontal, slightly low medium shot of the Noxian Magistrate behind the bench, armored in black iron, filling the frame with bulk and authority. He produces a pair of very small reading glasses and perches them carefully on his nose. He looks down at his papers and begins reading the charges. Ending composition: the magistrate mid-sentence in his tiny glasses, eyes on the page, as he is cut off.

dialogue.speaker: MAGISTRATE
dialogue.text: You entered Noxus under suspicious circumstances—

shots.atmosphere: Formal and imposing, undercut by the delicate glasses.
shots.music: None, or a faint low drone of officialdom.

intent.purpose: Deliver the escalation and reveal of the true charge.
intent.reason: One continuous two-shot keeps the interruptions and reactions in real time, without speaker-change cuts.
intent.attention: Riley's quick concession, then her reaction to the Lux charge.
intent.relationships: Riley prefers being an illegal intruder to being judged for her lane pick.

staging.positions: The magistrate is foreground at the bench; Riley faces him from the podium.
staging.eyelines: Riley looks up at the magistrate; he keeps reading his paper.
staging.camera: A static over-the-shoulder two-shot favouring Riley.

editorial.cutIn: Cut on Riley's interruption, reversing from the magistrate's single.
editorial.cutOut: Cut out to the onlookers' angle as a spectator leans in.
editorial.timing: Quick pickup on the second charge, then a beat of panic before her deflection.

advanced.longTakeIdea: Shots 3 and 4 could play as one continuous over-the-bench take if a later edit needs fewer cuts.

shots.title: Top Lane
shots.sourceExcerpt:
### RILEY

That’s fair.

### MAGISTRATE

—and knowingly selected Lux for the top lane.

### RILEY

I’d like to focus on the first thing.
shots.description: Opening composition: over the magistrate's iron-clad shoulder, looking across the bench at Riley behind the podium, framed as a two-shot. Riley readily concedes the first charge. The magistrate continues reading without pause and delivers the second charge. Riley's composure slips, and she quickly tries to steer back to the lesser offence. Ending composition: Riley in the frame's centre, hopeful and evasive, with the magistrate's shoulder and glasses edge in the foreground.

dialogue.speaker: MAGISTRATE
dialogue.text: —and knowingly selected Lux for the top lane.

dialogue.speaker: RILEY
dialogue.text: I’d like to focus on the first thing.

shots.atmosphere: A deadpan comic exchange; the real crime is revealed as the more embarrassing one.

intent.purpose: Make the trial public and Riley's shame visible.
intent.reason: The citizens' perspective places the audience among the judging crowd.
intent.attention: The spectator leaning in, then Riley's avoidance.
intent.relationships: The crowd is curious, and Riley wishes she were invisible.

staging.positions: The citizens are foreground at the edge of the square; Riley is behind them at the podium.
staging.eyelines: The spectator stares at Riley; Riley glances, then looks away.
staging.movement: The spectator leans forward; Riley shifts sideways behind the podium.
staging.camera: A static frame from behind the citizens.

editorial.cutIn: Cut on her deflection to the people witnessing it.
editorial.cutOut: Cut to the guard as he offers the next piece of evidence.

shots.title: Public Scrutiny
shots.sourceExcerpt: A spectator leans closer. Riley shifts behind the podium, avoiding their gaze.
shots.description: Opening composition: from among the three citizens at the square's edge, with their shoulders and heads in the foreground and Riley at the podium in the middle distance. One spectator leans conspicuously closer. Riley notices and shifts behind the podium, turning her face away to avoid their gaze. Ending composition: Riley half-hidden behind the podium, the leaning spectator dominating the foreground.
shots.atmosphere: Mild public embarrassment under bright light.

intent.purpose: Reveal what her team needed and gain Riley's commitment.
intent.reason: Keeping the guard and Riley together in depth links the evidence directly to her answer.
intent.attention: The guard's flat delivery, then Riley's hasty reply behind him.
intent.relationships: The team's plea is delivered secondhand; Riley tries to redeem herself.

staging.positions: The guard is seated in the foreground beside the podium; Riley stands behind the podium in the background.
staging.eyelines: The guard looks at his statement; Riley looks toward the bench.

editorial.cutIn: Cut from the crowd to the guard as he speaks.
editorial.cutOut: Cut on Riley's line to the magistrate's judging look.
editorial.timing: Leave a short pause after the quote before Riley answers.

shots.title: The Team's Statement
shots.sourceExcerpt:
### GUARD

Her team’s statement: “Please. We need someone to stand in front.”

### RILEY

I can stand in front.
shots.description: Opening composition: a medium shot of the seated guard in the foreground in profile, with Riley visible behind him at the podium. Without looking up, the guard reads her team's statement flatly. Behind him, Riley absorbs the plea and answers, a little too quickly. Ending composition: Riley in the background, having just spoken, the guard unmoved in the foreground.

dialogue.speaker: GUARD
dialogue.text: Her team’s statement: “Please. We need someone to stand in front.”

shots.atmosphere: Deadpan testimony with a touch of pathos from the absent team.

intent.purpose: Test Riley's claim and force her to live up to it.
intent.reason: The high, judging angle makes the magistrate's silent scrutiny the pressure that makes her straighten.
intent.attention: The magistrate's peering look, then Riley's slow straightening.
intent.relationships: His authority demands proof; she grudgingly accepts the front-line role.

staging.positions: The magistrate is at the bench; Riley is at the podium below his eyeline.
staging.eyelines: The magistrate looks down over his glasses at Riley; Riley looks up, then straightens.
staging.movement: Riley rises from a hunched to an upright posture.
staging.camera: A static high angle from behind the magistrate.

editorial.cutIn: Cut on Riley's claim to the judge weighing it.
editorial.cutOut: Scene end; hold after she straightens.
editorial.timing: A held, silent beat before she straightens, then a brief hold to end.

advanced.assumptions: Peering 'over the podium' is read as a downward look from the elevated bench.

shots.title: Stand Up Straight
shots.sourceExcerpt: The magistrate peers at her over the podium. She reluctantly straightens.
shots.description: Opening composition: a high angle from just behind the magistrate's head, looking down over his tiny glasses at Riley shrunk behind the podium. He lowers his head slightly, peering at her over the podium. Under his gaze, Riley reluctantly straightens to her full height. Ending composition: Riley upright behind the podium, held in the magistrate's looming high-angle view.
shots.music: A small, wry button: a single low brass note.

strategies.dramaticProgression: A deadpan trial. The scale is set by Noxus's looming power, then shrunk to petty absurdity. Riley's failed escape establishes that she cannot leave. The charges escalate from a serious one (suspicious entry) to the one she truly fears (picking Lux top lane). Public scrutiny and her own team's testimony corner her. She ends by making a reluctant, comic commitment to stand in front.
strategies.visualProgression: Open grand and imperial with the fortress over the square. Tighten into a lateral comic tableau for the escape gag. Isolate the magistrate's tiny glasses for authority undercut by absurdity. Play the charge exchange in an over-the-bench two-shot so interruptions land in real time. Widen briefly to the crowd's perspective for exposure. Bring the guard forward for the testimony. Close on a high, judging angle down at Riley as she straightens.
strategies.audienceInformation: The audience learns where we are (Noxus), that Riley is a reluctant defendant, and that she cannot slip away. The second charge reveals the real offence is a gaming-style lane pick. Her team's plea reveals what was expected of her. Riley's final line shows she will accept that role, however unwillingly.
strategies.spatialAnchors: The black fortress with crimson banners stands above the rooftops behind the bench. The magistrate's bench faces the battered defendant's podium. The guard's chair sits beside the podium, near the open passage. Three citizens watch from the edge of the sunlit square.
